transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [name]. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you. Um… I guess what finally made me make the appointment is that I’m having a really hard time keeping up with basic adult things. Like paying bills on time, replying to interview emails, remembering appointments, finishing errands I said I’d do… and I don’t mean to be irresponsible, but it’s started actually costing me opportunities. I kept thinking I could just try harder or get more organized, but it’s getting embarrassing, honestly.
Have you struggled with this kind of forgetfulness and difficulty finishing tasks since you were a kid, or is this more of a new pattern that started recently?

I think it’s been there since I was little, yeah. I mean, I did okay in school, so I don’t want to make it sound like I was a terrible student or anything, but even in elementary school my teachers would write things like I was bright, but I was always losing worksheets or not following the directions carefully.

I remember my desk being… really messy, like I couldn’t find assignments when I needed them. And I’d rush through things or talk out of turn sometimes. So I guess it isn’t totally new, it’s just become harder to cover for now.
Over the past two weeks, have you been feeling down, depressed, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day?

Um… I don’t think so. Not most of the day nearly every day, no. I’ve definitely felt frustrated and kind of embarrassed about all of this, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been depressed or hopeless like that. Is that… does that answer it?
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things—like your health, work, or everyday matters—more days than not, and having a hard time controlling that worry?

I don’t think so, not in that constant way. I mean, I worry about things when I’ve messed something up or I’m behind, but I wouldn’t say I’m worrying about everything more days than not. At least… I don’t think that’s the main issue. Does that make sense?
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or have trouble sitting still for long periods, or find yourself interrupting others or acting impulsively?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I try not to be distracting, but sitting still for a long time is really hard for me. Like in an interview or a meeting, or even during a movie, I get this feeling inside like I need to move or shift around or do something with my hands. If I can’t, it’s like I’m going to crawl out of my skin a little.

I don’t know if that sounds dramatic, but that’s kind of what it feels like.

Would you say these difficulties with organization, forgetfulness, and restlessness show up in multiple areas of your life—like at work, at home, and in your relationships—or is it mostly limited to one setting?

Yeah… unfortunately it’s not just one place. I wish it was, because then I could maybe fix that one thing.

Since I got fired, it’s been showing up in a lot of basic life stuff. Like I’ve missed follow-up emails for interviews, or I’ll mean to respond and then realize too much time has passed. And I had to step back from a volunteer project I really cared about because I just wasn’t keeping up reliably.

So… I’m not trying to make it sound worse than it is, but right now I’m unemployed and it feels like I can’t consistently manage the steps I’m supposed to take to move forward. Does that answer what you mean by multiple areas?

Thinking back to before you were about 12 years old, can you recall specific examples—like losing homework, being unable to sit still in class, or blurting out answers—that show these problems were already present that early?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I was a bad kid or anything, because I did pretty well in some ways. Teachers would usually say I was bright.

But I do remember report cards or comments saying I lost worksheets a lot, or I’d rush through directions and miss parts of what I was supposed to do. And I definitely got told I was talking out of turn. My desk was kind of… embarrassingly messy, like I couldn’t find assignments even when I had done them.

So yes, I think it was there pretty early, even in elementary school. Does that count as the kind of examples you mean?

Have you ever had a distinct period—lasting several days or more—where you felt unusually elated, full of energy, or needed much less sleep than normal, along with being more impulsive or talkative than usual?

I don’t think so… not in a clear way like that.

I mean, I’ve had times where I stayed up too late or got kind of excited about something and talked a lot, but I don’t think I’ve had several days where I felt unusually amazing or barely needed sleep and was just… way more impulsive than normal. At least not that I can recognize.

I’m not sure if I’m answering that correctly, but nothing really stands out to me like a distinct episode.
Do you regularly use caffeine, nicotine, or any other substances—prescribed or recreational—that might affect your concentration or energy levels?

Um… I don’t think there’s anything major there. I don’t want to give you the wrong answer, though.

I mean, I might have caffeine sometimes, like normal stuff, but I haven’t really tracked whether it changes my concentration or energy. And I’m not using anything else that I think would explain it.

Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
Do you often find your mind wandering or getting easily distracted by things going on around you, even when you're trying hard to focus on a task or conversation?

Yeah… I think so. I try not to blame everything on distractions, but it does happen a lot.

Like, I’ll sit down to update my resume or do a coding practice problem, and I really do mean to focus. But then a text notification pops up, or I hear someone talking outside, or even just a random thought like, “Oh, I should do that other thing,” and suddenly I’m completely off track. Sometimes I don’t even notice I’ve switched until several minutes later.

I don’t know if that’s more than normal, but it feels pretty hard to stay with the one task even when I’m trying.
